original_question: Let X_n be the random variable equal to the number of parking sequences with n drivers that succeed on a uniformly chosen labelled unordered tree T of size n. Beyond the known first-moment asymptotic E(X_n) = F_n / T_n, can one determine higher moments of X_n or obtain nontrivial information about the full distribution of X_n?
target_in_paper: Section 3, open problem (7) in the list of open problems from Lackner and Panholzer reproduced immediately after Corollary 4.11: the random variable counting parking functions for a uniformly chosen labelled unordered tree, whose expectation is known from previous enumeration results, but whose higher moments/distribution are not.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right open problem: it concerns a random variable counting successful parking assignments on a uniformly chosen labelled unordered tree of size n, asks about going beyond the first moment, and focuses on higher moments and distributional information. It also uses the same basic expectation ratio F_n/T_n that the paper mentions.
missing_details: The paper phrases the object as the number of parking functions for the random tree, not just 'parking sequences'; for a stand-alone question, it is best to say these are length-n preference sequences for which all n drivers successfully park on the tree.
The expectation identity E[X_n] = F_n/T_n is presented as an exact consequence of the earlier counting results, not merely as an asymptotic.

The notation F_n and T_n should be defined explicitly: F_n is the total number of tree parking functions when the number of parking spaces equals the number of drivers n, and T_n is the number of labelled unordered trees of size n.

The rooted-tree convention is implicit from the preceding definitions of tree parking functions; a stand-alone formulation should make clear that the parking problem is posed on the rooted/ordered-toward-the-root version of the labelled unordered tree.
The paper asks for 'higher moments or other results on the distribution' of X_n; asking for the 'full distribution' is slightly stronger than the official wording.
The scope should remain exactly this model: uniformly random labelled unordered trees of size n with n drivers, not arbitrary m-driver variants or other tree families.
refined_question: For each n >= 1, choose uniformly at random a rooted labelled unordered tree T with n vertices, and let X_n be the number of length-n preference sequences that are tree parking functions for T, i.e. for which all n drivers successfully park on T under the tree parking rule. If F_n denotes the total number of such tree parking functions over all rooted labelled unordered trees of size n and T_n denotes the total number of rooted labelled unordered trees of size n, so that E[X_n] = F_n/T_n exactly, can one determine higher moments of X_n, or at least obtain further nontrivial information about the distribution of X_n?
justification: The draft is targeting the seventh open problem listed in Section 3 of the survey. That item is the unique place where the paper introduces a random variable counting parking functions for a randomly chosen labelled unordered tree and explicitly says that, although the expectation follows from previous counting results, the approach does not yield higher moments or other distributional information. Your draft is already close, but it should be tightened in three ways to match the paper exactly: replace the 'first-moment asymptotic' by the exact identity E[X_n] = F_n/T_n, use the paper's terminology of parking functions, and avoid strengthening 'other results on the distribution' to the broader demand for the full distribution. The rooted-tree setup is also inherited from the nearby definitions and should be made explicit in a stand-alone restatement.
